summary: feat(doctor): report a newer release and a binary older than the installed skills require (issue #32)
reason: A host ran one release behind for two months while the skills on disk, symlinked from a clone, described the next one; nothing said so and the skill fell back to doing by hand what the newer binary does. The skills then carried a manual version check against the releases API, a step an agent can skip. The generated internal/cli/doctor.go carries two lines: addVersionChecks(cmd.Context(), report) where the report's version is set, and renderVersionChecks(w, report) in the human output. The hand-authored internal/cli/version_check.go does the work. latestRelease asks https://api.github.com/repos/nytafar/fiken-cli/releases/latest with a three second timeout and a User-Agent of the CLI name and version only, caches the answer for a day under the user cache dir (fiken-cli/latest-release.json), and returns nothing on any failure, with FIKEN_NO_UPDATE_CHECK set, or under PRINTING_PRESS_VERIFY, so doctor never hangs or fails because GitHub did. The report gains latest_release (absent when unknown), update_available, upgrade_command when behind, and skills[]: every installed skill whose frontmatter name is `fiken` or starts with `fiken-`, found under FIKEN_SKILLS_ROOT, ~/.claude/skills, ~/.agents/skills and ./.claude/skills (a symlinked skill reachable from two roots is listed once), each with `requires` read from frontmatter metadata.fiken-cli.requires and `satisfied`. Versions compare numerically; an unreadable version is never called old. The generated version command is not edited: novel_commands.go calls addVersionCheckFlag, which adds --check to it from outside and leaves plain `version` printing what it did. Both skills in this repo state metadata.fiken-cli.requires, and a test fails if one omits it or names a version newer than the code's.
validated_outcome: make check green. internal/cli/version_check_test.go empties the release URL for the whole test binary, so no test reaches GitHub; the lookup tests point it at an httptest server. They cover numeric version comparison, the frontmatter reader (another tool's `requires` and a top-level one are not read), skill discovery across roots with a symlinked skill listed once, the one-day cache (one request within 23 hours, a second after 25), silent failure on a 403, an unreachable host and the disable variable, the report fields when behind and when offline, `doctor --json` carrying latest_release, update_available and per-skill requires/satisfied, and that this repo's skills state a minimum version no newer than the code's.
